message.source: KEYS Space the leader card, in Normal mode: a key runs its command (its list is the card); Ctrl+Space opens it in every editor mode Ctrl+G, SPC /, SPC SPC search the workspace, by words and meaning: the hits on the left, the file on the right at the hit; beneath, a checkbox per stage it can run (Lexical; Semantic with a model in use; Rerank, naming the ranker, with one in use): a change searches again, and one of Lexical and Semantic stays checked / find a word in the pane with the keyboard (the page, the explorer, the links); n and N find it again, forward and back. In the page its words are marked, and "finding …" shows at the top right: its ✕ clears it, as Search › Clear find does. In the Text mode / types a slash: Search › Find in page, Find next, Find previous * # in the page, in Vim's Normal mode, find the word under the cursor, whole, on or back (g* g# as part of a word too): it becomes the page's find, so n and N go on SPC o open a document: a filter over the workspace's files, with a preview SPC b the buffer card: 1 to 9 show the 1st to the 9th buffer in the tabs' order (H and L's), 0 the 10th; d closes the one shown (File › Close buffer, :bd), asking first over unsaved changes; r and l close the buffers to its right and left, nearest first, each asked about as d asks: a Stay stops there, that buffer shown; s switches buffer (Go › Buffers…, :b), the open files and drafts each previewed with its unsaved text; b goes back H L in the page, in Vim's Normal mode, the buffer before or after the shown one, in the order of the GUI's tabs, wrapping (bufferline's Shift+h / Shift+l): this replaces Vim's H and L (the screen's top and bottom line) in Normal mode only; Visual mode keeps them, and Insert mode types them. A script's own H or L (autodoc.map) wins Ctrl+O Ctrl+I back and forward along the jumps (Vim's jump list, in Normal mode): a link followed, a document opened from a picker, the explorer, the links or the recent files, and the page's own jumps (G, gg, %, { }, a mark's). Back to another document opens it where you left it, in the view you left it in SPC f open a file anywhere on the disk (File › Open file…), with a preview: one in a workspace's folder opens there; any other is in no workspace, so it has no search, links, backlinks, frontmatter check or embeddings (the status line says so) SPC r the recent files, the newest first, of every workspace (File › Recent files…); one of another workspace opens there SPC d view the Mermaid diagram at the cursor (File › Preview Mermaid diagram…; the editor's right-click View diagram) SPC H preview the note as HTML (File › Preview HTML) File › Open with Default App the file in the desktop's default app: a PDF in its reader, for what its derived text cannot show Ctrl+N new file, in any folder (File › New file…; SPC n); .md added when it has none Ctrl+S save the file Ctrl+; the command line, in every editor mode (:, in Vim's Normal mode): :w, :find, :table, your Lua commands … (Search › Command line…; a terminal needs kitty's keyboard protocol to send Ctrl+;) Ctrl+W switch workspace (SPC w too); Manage… adds, renames and deletes them. In the Vim editor mode's Insert, Ctrl+W is Vim's: it deletes the word before the cursor (Esc first to switch). Insert's Ctrl+U deletes back to the indent, and Ctrl+O runs one Normal-mode command Ctrl+h/j/k/l in Normal mode, to the open panel on that side, and back to the page; in the terminal and agent panels too, while typing (Options › Terminal turns that off), and arriving there by one of them you type at once F6 and Shift+F6 the next or the previous open widget: the editor and the panels, never the menu bar. SPC Tab, or :go <name>, goes to one by name (Go › Widget…) F10, Alt+letter the menu bar, which hides until then (Options › Editor preferences can keep it). SPC m show and focus the menu bar; again hides it On a Mac, Option+letter is Alt+letter (US layout; Option+E, I, N, U are dead keys there), and F10 may need Fn SPC k the editor mode: Vim (modal) or Text (modeless, an ordinary text editor's keys) ? the Vim keys' card, at the bottom right (Normal mode); ? again closes it SPC h the notifications' history (Go › Notifications…) F11, SPC M maximize or restore the terminal or the agents (the one with the keyboard, in a shell too, else the newest open), as their tab menu's Maximize: a program in a panel never gets F11; a terminal emulator that takes F11 itself (GNOME Terminal's full screen) keeps it: SPC M always works Ctrl+Tab and Ctrl+Shift+Tab the next or the previous tab of the terminal or the agents (the one with the keyboard), round; its program never gets them (Ctrl+\ first sends one). message.source: THE LAYOUT The page is a window of its own, and each panel (the explorer, the terminal, the agent, the results and the todos) floats over it or is tiled beside it, as its Layout says. Layout › Tiled or Float is on every window's menu, right above Go to ›: the page's buffer strip, the terminal's and the agent's tabs, the explorer's and the todos' ≡, and the end of the results table's right-click menu. :layout [window] opens it over the page, the page's alone (Tab lists the windows). The page is tiled unless you float it; every panel floats unless you tile it. A tiled panel sits at the edge its Layout › Tiled › names (Left, Right, Top or Bottom), a share of the base across it (the preferences tui.<window>.tileEdge and tui.<window>.tileSize); Alt and a right drag move the border it shares, and its new share is kept. When the window is too small for the page and the panels tiled, the panel tiled last floats until the room comes back, then tiles again by itself: its Layout stays Tiled. A floating page moves and resizes up to the page's width, never closes, and comes forward when it takes the keyboard; when it is minimized, the dock's editor icon shows it again. Ctrl+h/j/k/l go to the window placed that way, tiled, docked or floating alike. Arrange panel (SPC L) moves a floating or docked panel; a tiled one is placed by its tile.

message.source:
THE PAGE The file is a page 120 columns wide, centred, the ruler at its edge (Preferences sets the width). In the Vim editor mode, i types and Esc goes back to Normal; in the Text mode, typing types. With no file open, the page is an untitled draft: type, and Ctrl+S names and saves it. The status line (SPC t) shows the mode, the file, and [+] while it has unsaved changes, and on its right what the page says (a find's result). The page's frame shows where the cursor is: the headings above it in Markdown, the key path in YAML. SPC O (Go › Outline…) lists the file's headings, unsaved ones too; Enter jumps there. Long lines wrap at the page's width, and line numbers can show: View › Wrap long lines, Line numbers, or Preferences. A PDF or DOCX opens as its derived text, read-only, where the daemon's build derives it: the frame and the status line say [PDF · read-only]. Motions, find, copy and the outline work; edits and saves do not. File › Open with Default App opens the original. A long one shows as much as one read carries, and says where it was cut. An HTML file asks first: Simplified, its derived text read-only as above, or Raw, the HTML itself to edit and save. In the GUI a raw file's Rendered view (Ctrl+T) is its page: j k or the arrows scroll, Ctrl+D Ctrl+U half a page, g G the ends, and its links open as notes, files or the browser. Its stylesheets and images load from its workspace (a file outside every workspace: its own folder only; add the folder as a workspace for a site sharing ../assets).
